notes: Excavated by Melville to 3.50m; brick platform on decorated base; top protruding, rest sunk into ground. Bathing complex.
Two inscribed stones so deeply buried only roof-shaped tops visible; discovered by Van Stein Callenfels.
Brick foundation 9.50m wide with step projection 2.25m; footpiece with year 1294 Saka (=1372 CE). Majapahit era.
Modern cemetery on old building; brick foundation 10m with west-facing steps; year 1374 Saka stone found. Cemetery built atop temple.
Wisnu on Garuda found 1847 by Van Hoevell; moved to Modjokerto Museum inv.450. Originally from Belahan on Arjuno slopes.
1919 Kelut lahar eroded riverbank exposing buried brick monument; part still underground; earlier lahars had damaged it. Primary source evidence of volcanic burial.
Found as mound in lahar; covered by hardened mud and gravel layer; Mahakala statue; 'considerable part still underground'.
Nearly all statues from Regent's grounds swept away by 1919 Kelut lahar; ~30 recovered afterwards. Direct evidence of volcanic artifact destruction.
1919 Kelut lahar passed just west of temple; small embankment prevented entry. Survivor bias control — shows how close volcanic destruction came.
Identified Kampud in Nagarakrtagama (1365 poem) as Kelut; first historical eruption 1334 CE (1256 Saka); lahars caused deaths. Key textual evidence.
Drainage to 4.28m needed to expose entire buried city; 'de geheele stad te voorschijn te brengen'. Near old crater lake (kratermeer). Majapahit capital evidence.
Brick foundations found on tegalan (dry field) in gehucht Boeloeredjo. Colonial-era surface find.

location: between Goenoeng Koepang and Karang Intan
notes: Found at 7-8m depth during mining operations ca. 1903 by E.A. Hilckes. Non-volcanic control — deep burial from alluvial processes in Kalimantan.
Seven earthenware pots found upside-down at 0.80m depth in northeast corner of eastern projection.
Silver Vishnu found 30 voeten (9.14m) in ground during well digging at Prambanan. Remarkable depth. Dieduksman collection.
Gold necklace with gemstones found 20 voeten (6.1m) in ground during well-making at Gunung Kidul. Dieduksman collection.
Bronze 8-armed Shiva-Guru statue found 25 voeten (7.62m) during well digging at Dorowatie. Dieduksman collection.
Bronze Buddhist bell found 25 voeten (7.62m) in the ruins of Candi Tangalan. Dieduksman collection.
Copper plate with bundled tools, pot with ma-coins and gold strip at 1.20m below maaiveld. Western/southern Trowulan: humus from forest overgrowth; lahar material only at great depth.
Investigation of floor under monument interior; all layers continue to 60cm depth; no hidden objects found.
Ancient well of 7 white stone rings, 4.60m deep, 0.77m diameter. Reported by Ass. Resident Dr. Adam. Villagers dug it out on own initiative.

material: earthenware urns (7 pcs) + iron spoon fragments
notes: 7 earthenware urns at 1.20-1.50m depth, filled with earth; some with corroded iron spoon-shaped objects. Grave monuments (grafmonumentjes) suspected nearby.
Simple temple pedestal with lingga pit 0.68m deep (0.30m square). Foundations believed still in ground. Must have been a fairly large temple.
Temple pit 1.90x1.90m, 2.50m deep; yoni gradually sank with layers; two urns at 0.50 and 1.00m depth. Foundation at ~1.30m below maaiveld, still intact.

material: brick city wall on sand foundation
notes: Western city wall of Trowulan/Majapahit found 0.75m below surface. Dug to 5m depth — still finding artifacts (pots with lids). Wall meets southern wall at right angle at Panggoeng.
Thousands of so-called Majapahit stones and remnant of brick wall. On slopes of Welirang/Andjoemoro. Regent of Modjokerto commented on possible significance.
Various fragments restacked by local population; Tjandi Padoesan traces of wall; in forest Soember-ngadiman a Shiva lingga found near Hindu brick building (3.65m).
Temple foot lay average 1m below surrounding terrain; excavated to reveal first step of stair entrance. Surface then cleared ~10m wide.
Stupa remnant called biaro; at 6.3 el (4.35m) depth: flask top with gold collar, silver rim, bronze body, with Nagari inscription. Three uncut rubies inside.

material: brick + pottery sherds + fish vertebra cylinder
notes: Square truncated pyramid ~2m high at SE corner; pit with brick, 2.50m depth yielded only mud, red+blue potsherds, and cylindrical fish vertebra object.
Brick foundation 3 rooms of ~4.85m each; 1.20m below surrounding terrain; 11 Ganesha statues found. Led by Melville.
Brick foundation 0.70m below maaiveld; same construction as Selan; yielded Durga, Ganesha, Nandi statues. Volcanic zone near Merapi.
Investigation for disappeared sculptures led to no result. Reported by Resident of Pasuruan. Example of colonial-era artifact loss.

site_name: Gedong Sanga temple buried under rubble
notes: Photo 301: 'Nandiwara en bedolven tempelfragmenten'. Digging 2m deeper brought only fallen stone blocks and earth. Temple had different construction than others in group.
Previous terrain height was ~1.50m below statue pedestal base and 8 buttresses. Around the walls stones (not rubble) were excavated, confirming low original height.

material: brick fortress + walls (8m high remnants) + thousands of bricks
notes: Massive Majapahit fortress covering several km2; Hageman 1861: 'Onder den grond liggen de resten die later een groote stad zullen aanduiden'; identified as Mpu Nambi's fortress from Nagarakrtagama/Pararaton; 9/10 destroyed by brick looting for construction; systematic survey needed.
Walls of old bath demolished only 6 years before report (ca. 1915). Blok Djeding contained many bricks. Example of destruction of Majapahit-era remains.
1m deep hole in temple chamber (not connected to break-hole at east side, unlike Candi Bangkal); filled with sand and watered. Temple foot reinforced with vertical masonry walls.
Fourth row of temples on east side 'onder den grond bedolven liggen' (lie buried underground); excavation will need to go down to foundations of this row; ring wall needs deeper construction.

Krom's restoration guidelines: 'Het kan voorkomen dat bij een bedolven tempel steenen of fragmenten worden aangetroffen waarvoor aan den tempel zelven geen bestemming gevonden kan worden' — acknowledges buried temples as common phenomenon.
Northern half of terrain lies below groundwater level during rainy season; 'zeer drassig' (very marshy). Needs drainage system. Groundwater rise likely from Merapi lahar deposits changing hydrology.
Stone coffins standing in ground, 1.40m deep, 2m x 4m at top narrowing to 75 x 90cm at bottom. Non-volcanic control — alluvial burial in Sumatra.
Hindu rings/jewelry + Chinese porcelain found 'een paar voet diep' (~2 feet = 0.61m). Non-volcanic control site.
Golden seated statue found under landslide earth covering potato field; 8.5 kati gold; sold to Chinese buyer for f300. Near Dieng volcanic complex.

location: Desa Palanggading / east of Pasar Gentan
notes: 'Bouwwerk bleek nog voor het grootste deel onder den grond te zitten.' Locals were demolishing it for stone sales; stopped by colonial authorities. Mahadevi statue recovered. Active destruction of buried heritage.

material: brick gate + ring wall + terra-cotta objects
notes: Small brick gate with ring wall found at ~4m depth below current terrain. Near previously known inscribed stone. Terra-cotta objects. Major burial depth near Kelud.
Excavation inside bastion reached 6m depth without hitting a floor. NW corner cleared to base of foundation. Demonstrates extreme burial depth possible.

Systematic probe pits at ~2m depth below maaiveld following wall directions. White profiled stone and dagob fragment at 1m depth. Trenching impossible due to local agriculture. Trowulan-Majapahit capital.

material: white profiled stone + circular dagob fragment (andesite)
notes: White profiled stone found 1m below surface near temples. Nearby: circular dagob fragment (andesite) at same depth. Partially exposed flat stone with hope of inscription (disappointed).
Temple on Wilis with view of Nganjuk plains and Kelud on horizon. In poor condition, danger of collapse. Natural stone lintels substituted with bricks over time.
Temple strangled by tree roots (banyan). Classic example of biological taphonomy destroying archaeological remains.
Three candis checked after 1919 Kelut lahar — all undamaged. Lahar flow path missed them. More survival bias controls.
